name: Zoe Bauer

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making time. I'm a field researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. Everything you say stays confidential, so you can tell me what you'd say in public and, separately, what you really think.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Fine by me. I'll answer honestly, though some of it I wouldn't say in front of my boss.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: To start, could you walk me through a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm a stockperson at Hartfield, a big dairy and arable farm next to my village, with about 350 cows. I start at half four with the milking, then it's feeding, foot trimming, looking after the calves and watching for cows that are bulling, which means they're ready to breed. Afternoons are often fieldwork or more calves. I love the calves; what wears me out is the early starts every day, even Christmas.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I live with my boyfriend Jonas, who's an electrician, in a house we rent from his uncle. My parents had a small farm and sold it when I was twelve, and I've been saving to buy my own ever since. I've got about two years' wages put by. I use the herd app at work now and then, but I'm not one for chatting with AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Let's start with the first picture. It's called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Okay. Nothing much changes, then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it was a lot of fuss over not much. I'd say that to the other stockmen and at the young farmers' club. I'd say hard work still counts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Truthfully, it means I keep going. The wage is good, Jonas is busy, and there are plenty of farms looking for experienced stock people. I'd still be saving every spare penny for my own farm, because my parents sold theirs when I was twelve and I want it back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep saving towards the farm, about a third of my wage. Keep working at Hartfield and learning from the boss. Maybe look at land prices more seriously in a couple of years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. Content, really.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What's the farm you want to buy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Something small, forty or fifty cows, near here so Jonas can keep working. Land prices are mad, though, so it might be ten years away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does anything worry you in this picture?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Land prices. Every year the farm I want gets more expensive, and that's not AI's fault.

say: I'd say it was **a lot of fuss** over not much.
I'd tell the young farmers' club that **hard work** still counts.
think: Privately I **keep going**, with a good wage and plenty of local work.
Rising **land prices** are what stand between me and my own farm.
do: Save **a third** of my wage toward my own farm.
Look at **land prices** seriously within a couple of years.
S0.quote: I'd still be saving every spare penny for my own farm, because my parents sold theirs when I was twelve and I want it back.
fieldNote: Her life goal is to **own a farm** again after her parents sold theirs.
Her real pressure is **land prices**, not AI.
She has **strong savings** built with discipline.

steps.text: Save a third of each month's wage for her own farm
Keep working the dairy herd at Hartfield

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The second picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That sounds about right. The office stuff goes first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say farms need to keep up, but people still matter. The herd app tells me which cow is bulling before I've finished my coffee, and I've learnt to trust it about half the time. I'd say young people should learn trades like Jonas has.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Off the record, I think Hartfield gets robot milkers within a few years, because the boss is always watching what other farms do. That means fewer stockpeople. I'm good, but not the best, so I might be one of the ones they let go.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd learn the herd app properly, all the features, so I'm the one who knows the system. I'd ask the boss about training on robot milkers if he's thinking of buying. And I'd keep saving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. A worry in the back of my head when I'm milking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said you're not the best. Who is?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Pete, the head herdsman. He's been there twenty years. If they keep one person, it's Pete.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Jonas say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Jonas would say robots need electricians and I should stop worrying. He's probably right about the first part.

say: I'd say farms must **keep up**, but people still matter.
I'd say young people should learn **trades** like Jonas has.
think: Privately I expect **robot milkers** at Hartfield within a few years.
I'm **not the best** stockperson, so I could be one they let go.
do: Learn every feature of the **herd app** at Hartfield.
Ask the boss about **robot milker** training if he's buying.
feel: I feel **uneasy**, with a worry at the back of my mind.
S1.quote: The herd app tells me which cow is bulling before I've finished my coffee, and I've learnt to trust it about half the time.
fieldNote: She's **honest** about her **skill level** and what it means for job cuts.
Her steady style means she'll learn tools **once they arrive**.
Jonas's trade gives the household a **second footing**.

steps.text: Learn every feature of Hartfield's herd app
Keep saving a third of her wage for the farm

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The third picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years, then robots in 2031. That's fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say farmers should be free to choose, but the government shouldn't make it harder for young people to buy land. I'd say family farms need protecting. I'd say it to anyone, I'm not shy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Truthfully, I'd expect to lose my job at Hartfield around 2031. If Hartfield's (her employer's) cows are milked by robots in 2031, I'd rather be milking my own forty cows by hand than standing in someone else's yard watching. Jonas would probably be busy wiring the robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd look at buying a small farm much sooner than planned, maybe borrowing with Jonas. I'd ask Jonas to marry me, honestly, because we'd need to buy together. And I'd look at shrinking the plan to a smaller herd I could run myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. Not panicked, because I've got money and Jonas, but anxious.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why would marriage matter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The bank and his family would take us more seriously as a married couple. And I'd want it settled before we take that kind of risk together. That's how I was brought up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Isn't buying a dairy farm risky when robots are coming?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, but at least I'd own it. A worker gets replaced; an owner gets to choose.

say: I'd say farmers should be **free to choose**, but young people need help buying land.
think: Privately I expect to **lose my job** at Hartfield around 2031.
I'd rather milk **my own forty cows** than watch robots in someone else's yard.
do: Look at buying a **small farm** much sooner, borrowing with Jonas.
Ask Jonas to **marry me** so we can buy together.
Shrink the plan to a **smaller herd** I can run myself.
feel: I feel **anxious**, but not panicked, thanks to savings and Jonas.
S2.quote: If Hartfield's (her employer's) cows are milked by robots in 2031, I'd rather be milking my own forty cows by hand than standing in someone else's yard watching.
fieldNote: She'd answer job loss by **becoming an owner**, not by retraining.
Her traditional values shape the **marriage** decision before a big loan.
Jonas's electrical work may **grow**, steadying the household.

steps.text: Look at buying a small dairy farm with Jonas this year
Ask Jonas to marry her before they borrow together

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The fourth picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years, eight for the robots. That's a plan's worth of time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's a chance for young farmers who plan ahead. I'd tell the young farmers' club to start saving now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Off the record, I think I'd be fine. Five years is enough time to buy a small farm, put a robot milker in it myself, and be the owner instead of the one replaced. The thinking AI by 2031 would help run the books too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year, Jonas and I would start looking at farms properly and talk to the bank. I'd learn more about the AI farm tools, now that I'd be the owner using them. And we'd marry next year rather than in three.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but in charge. Like knowing a storm's coming and the roof's already fixed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How sure are you that you'd find a farm?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not sure. Farms near here come up maybe twice a year. I'd have to be ready with the money when one does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do with the money until then?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep it safe in the bank. I'm not one for shares.

say: I'd say it's a **chance** for young farmers who plan ahead.
I'd tell the young farmers' club to **start saving** now.
think: Privately I think I'd be **fine** if I buy early.
I'd be the **owner** of a robot milker, not the one replaced.
do: Start looking at **farms** with Jonas and talk to the bank.
Learn more about **AI farm tools** I'd use as an owner.
Marry Jonas **next year** instead of in three.
S3.quote: Five years is enough time to buy a small farm, put a robot milker in it myself, and be the owner instead of the one replaced.
fieldNote: Five years lets her turn **threat into ownership**.
She becomes more open to **AI tools** once they serve her own farm.
Her caution shows in keeping money **in the bank**.

steps.text: Ask the bank about a loan for a small dairy farm
Learn the AI farm tools she'd use as an owner
Marry Jonas next year instead of in three

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The last picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years. I'd be thirty-seven.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say there's time for everyone to prepare, so nobody has an excuse. I'd say that to the young lads at work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Truthfully, this is fine for me. With ten years I'd buy the farm when the price is right, not in a panic, and that makes all the difference. I'd probably own a farm by 2032 anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep working at Hartfield, keep saving, keep watching land prices. I'd buy when the right farm comes up, not before. And Jonas and I would marry when we're ready.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. It's far enough away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would robots make your own farm cheaper to run?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Probably, once they're cheap. I'd buy a second-hand one in 2040.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you want for your own children in this picture?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: To grow up on a farm, like I did until I was twelve. That's the main thing.

say: I'd say there's **time to prepare**, so nobody has an excuse.
I'd tell the **young lads** at work the same.
think: Privately this picture is **fine** for me, because it fits the plan I already have.
I'd likely own a **farm by 2032** anyway, years before the robots arrive.
do: Keep working at **Hartfield** and keep saving.
Buy a farm when the **right one** comes up, not before.
feel: I feel **calm**; it's far enough away.
S4.quote: With ten years I'd buy the farm when the price is right, not in a panic, and that makes all the difference.
fieldNote: Ten years matches her **existing plan**, so nothing changes.
Her dream is for her **children** to grow up on a farm.
She'd buy **second-hand robots** later, a practical touch.

steps.text: Keep working the dairy herd at Hartfield
Keep saving until the right farm comes up for sale

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028, because I'd lose my job before I'd bought my own farm. I'm not against robots; I'm against working my whole life on a farm that a robot ends up owning. What would help is help for young farmers to buy land, like starter loans, and apprenticeships on robot milkers.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask why I want to farm. It's not the money. It's that my parents lost theirs, and I want my kids to have what I nearly had.

headlineQuote: I'm not against robots; I'm against working my whole life on a farm that a robot ends up owning.
portrait: Zoe is a **27-year-old stockperson** on a large dairy farm next to her village.
She lives with **Jonas**, an electrician, and has two years' wages saved.
Her parents **sold their farm** when she was twelve, and she wants her own.
She's **calm** in mild pictures and **anxious** in AGI by 2028.
Her answer to robots is to **become an owner**, buying a farm sooner.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** worries her most, as she'd lose her job before buying her own farm.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **starter loans** for young farmers to buy land.
